figures.title: Affine quantization: encode 0.05 and 0.2, decode them back
figures.caption: Affine quantization maps a group interval onto 16 unsigned codes with a scale s and a zero point z. For the group [−1, 1], s = 2/15 and z = 8: 0.05 encodes to code 8 and decodes to 0; 0.2 encodes to code 10 and decodes to 0.2667, an error of 0.0667. Every weight in the group pays at most half a step, and the bound is set by the group, not by the loudest number in the matrix.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. The encode panel gives the group range −1 to 1, scale s = 2/15, zero point 8, and the two encodings: 0.05 to code 8 and 0.2 to code 10. The decode panel reverses the map: code 8 to 0 and code 10 to 0.2667, so the 0.2 weight pays 0.0667, exactly the half-step bound. A note explains that the zero point lets the interval sit off zero and that only storage is four bits.

panels.title: Decode: q → ŵ
panels.note: The zero point keeps zero representable and spends levels where the values are. Only storage is four bits; the kernel subtracts z, multiplies by s, and converts to fp16 for the tensor-core multiply.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to encode and decode one group.

steps.label: Compute the scale s = 2/15 and the zero point z = 8.
Encode 0.05 to code 8 and 0.2 to code 10.
Decode code 8 to 0 and code 10 to 0.2667.
The 0.2 weight pays 0.0667, under the half-step bound.

figures.title: Groups run along the input dimension, so an outlier contaminates one group
figures.caption: W is d_out × d_in, stored row-major, so 128 consecutive input features in one row form a contiguous 64-byte read. Each cell here is one such group of 128 weights, and the ink is the group's largest absolute weight. A group carries 3 bytes of metadata against 64 bytes of payload: 4.7 percent overhead, or 4.19 bits per weight. The 4.0 outlier in group g3 of the first row sets that group's scale, so the other 127 entries round toward level 0. Isolating the outlier in its own group lets the remaining 127 resolve 0.1 to within 0.013.
figures.alt: A grid with four rows, one per output channel, and eight columns, one per group of 128 input features. Most cells hold 0.1 and draw a short bar; the cell in column g3 of the first row holds 4.0 and draws a full bar, marking the outlier group. The note explains that groups run along d_in because that is the contiguous 64-byte read, that 3 bytes of metadata cost 4.7 percent against 64 bytes of payload, and that the outlier sets the scale for its 127 neighbours.

data.note: Each cell is a group of 128 consecutive input features in one row of W; the ink is the group's largest |w|. Groups run along d_in so a group is a contiguous 64-byte read. A group carries 3 bytes of metadata against 64 bytes of payload, 4.7 percent overhead. The 4.0 outlier in the first row's g3 sets that group's scale; the other 127 entries collapse toward level 0.
